clue.text: Perceptive one just losing lead to trap bridge partners

indicators.note: to trap means to catch and hold, so the pair of letters is held within the rest

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: losing lead drops the first letter of the word

parts.note: rightful means just or legitimate
North and South are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A sharp player, just short of the lead, sets a trap for the partners across the bridge table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing lead' cuts RIGHTFUL to IGHTFUL; after I, 'to trap' holds NS inside. In bridge the four players are named by compass points, N and S being partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone insightful shows deep understanding, so is perceptive.

clue.text: Soldiers dividing in Asian country

indicators.note: something dividing a word splits it apart by sitting in its middle

parts.note: taken as written; it is the word being split
RA, the Royal Artillery, stands for soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are deployed to keep factions apart somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'in' is doing double duty as the fodder here: RA splits I and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in western Asia, so it is an example of an Asian country.

clue.text: Feeling nauseous taking part in burlesque — am I shameful?

indicators.note: the answer takes part in these words, spread across them as a run of consecutive letters

parts.note: the letters run from the end of burlesque through am and I into the start of shameful

explanation.surface: A performer in a risqué variety show feels queasy and wonders if the act is disgraceful.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash and question mark make it read as a confession, but the answer sits across three of those words.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeamish describes being easily sickened or queasy, a state close to feeling nauseous.

clue.text: Unfortunate leak at largest source of saline water

indicators.note: something unfortunate has gone wrong, so the letters that follow are knocked out of order

parts.note: all thirteen letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A bad leak has sprung at the biggest supplier of brine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largest' looks like part of the definition, but it belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Salt Lake in Utah is a huge salty lake, so it is a supply of brackish, salty water.

clue.text: Young swimmer thanks head of diving staff

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of diving
a staff is a pole or stick

explanation.surface: A youngster in the pool thanks the head of the diving staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' reads as employees, but here it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the larval form of a frog, a juvenile creature that lives and swims in water.

clue.text: A French film starring Liam Neeson is free

parts.note: un is French for a
Taken is the 2008 thriller starring Liam Neeson

explanation.surface: A French movie with Liam Neeson in it can be watched at no charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untaken, like a seat, has not been claimed, so it is still free or available.

clue.text: Keen poet gets top grade for first of odes

indicators.text: gets top grade for first of odes
indicators.note: the poet's name receives the highest mark in place of the letter that starts odes

parts.note: Ovid, the Roman poet

indicators.note: 'first of' keeps only the first letter of 'odes'

parts.note: the opening letter of odes, the letter swapped out
A is the highest grade

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic poet earns an A for his first odes.
explanation.walkthrough: Ovid's opening O is replaced by A, giving AVID.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid and keen are synonyms, both meaning eager and enthusiastic.

clue.text: Shade? Perhaps tourist ignores it

indicators.note: ignoring it means leaving out the two letters of the word it

parts.note: a tourist is an example of a visitor, hence perhaps
taken as written: the letters dropped

explanation.surface: Needing some shade, a tourist doesn't bother with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A visor is the brim on a cap that shields the eyes, so it gives shade.

clue.text: The German collecting a pile of leaves covering yard is one preoccupied

covering means wrapping around, so the paper pile surrounds the yard abbreviation

parts.note: der is German for the
taken as written
yd is the abbreviation for yard
a ream is a pile of paper leaves, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A German gathering a heap of autumn leaves across the yard is lost in thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' suggests autumn foliage but means sheets of paper; two containers nest, one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A daydreamer drifts off into thought, so is someone whose mind is preoccupied elsewhere.

clue.text: Blue laurel uncovered around eastern side of Oz

indicators.note: around has the stripped word wrapped round the single letter
uncovered strips the outer letters off the word

parts.note: laurel without its first and last letters leaves AURE

indicators.note: on a map the east is the right-hand side, so this is the last letter of the word

parts.note: the last letter of Oz is Z

explanation.surface: A blue-tinged laurel bush on the east coast of Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' leaves AURE from laurel; it goes 'around' Z, the right-hand, eastern end of Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: Azure is the clear bright blue of an unclouded sky.

clue.text: Obediently performing lousy duet

indicators.note: performing suggests putting something on in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: all nine letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: Two singers dutifully perform a poor duet.
explanation.definitionFit: Duteous is an old word for dutiful, so acting duteously means acting obediently.

clue.text: Nasty thing: bilge regularly discharged around Scottish island

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the island sits inside the other letters

parts.note: a thing is an object

indicators.note: letters discharged at regular intervals means every other one is thrown out

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of bilge
Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: Something foul: ship's bilge water being pumped out near a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: Bilge is the dirty water collecting in a ship's hull; 'regularly' keeps the odd-placed letters. The thing and the bilge letters together go around the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Objectionable means offensive or unpleasant, which is what nasty describes.

clue.text: Maybe sculpture of king couple stored in chest

indicators.note: items stored in a chest are put inside it, so these letters go within the box word

parts.note: an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant
R, from Rex, is the abbreviation for king
a couple is two

explanation.surface: A statue of a royal pair is kept in a strongbox.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculpture is one example of artwork, which the word maybe acknowledges.

clue.text: Person in court starts to judge umpire rashly over rulings

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the five words

explanation.definitionFit: A juror sits on a jury in a courtroom, so is one of the people present at a trial.

clue.text: Odd — graduate entered into GCSEs weirdly struggles

indicators.note: something entered into another word is placed inside it, so the two short pieces sit within the jumbled exam letters
weirdly means in a strange way, so the exam letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written; the fodder
rum is old British slang for odd or strange
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A strange tale of a university graduate sitting school exams and finding them hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: GCSEs are the exams English pupils take at about sixteen; 'Odd' reads as a comment, but it supplies rum.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrummage is to scuffle or jostle, as rugby forwards do in a scrum, so it means struggles.

clue.text: Invention from company, popular with time

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
in means fashionable or popular
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A firm's new product becomes a hit over time.
explanation.definitionFit: A coinage is a newly invented word or phrase, so it is an invention in language.

clue.text: New casino outside Italy's capital city

parts.note: taken as written; the fodder
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Italy's capital' looks like Rome or the letter I; the letter is right, and 'capital city' is the definition, sharing the word capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital of Cyprus, so it is an example of a capital city.

clue.text: Sole towel turned abrasive

indicators.note: turned means altered in form, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: all nine letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: The only towel available proved scratchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel wool is a pad of fine steel strands used for scouring, so it is an abrasive material.

clue.text: Release successful song when in band (not B-side)

indicators.note: when in places the song inside the shortened group
not says the letter is left out of the word

parts.note: a bunch is a band or group
the B of B-side is the letter dropped
a hit is a successful song

explanation.surface: A band put out a hit single with no B-side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks musical but means a bunch; with no B it is UNCH, and HIT goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhitch something is to unfasten it, so release it from what holds it.

clue.text: Grow disheartened in house with waste material and rubbish

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next word

parts.note: ho is the abbreviation for house
ash is what is left after burning

indicators.note: disheartened means having lost its heart, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of grow

explanation.surface: Living with piles of junk and garbage would make anyone despondent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grow disheartened' reads as feeling low, but it is an instruction to remove the heart of grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogwash is nonsense, originally pigswill, and rubbish is a common synonym for nonsense.

clue.text: Leading to Middle East, brief excursion on boat

indicators.note: leading to puts the pieces before the Middle East letters, which come last
brief cuts off the final letter

parts.note: a trip is an excursion
re means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A short boat trip heading towards the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' trims TRIP to TRI, and RE (on) follows; this 'leading to' ME closes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient galley warship with three banks of oars.

clue.text: Take advantage of time with great energy supplier

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
rad is slang for great or excellent
E.ON is a large energy supplier in Britain

explanation.surface: Making the most of a period with a top power company.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade on something is to exploit it for gain, so it means to take advantage of it.

clue.text: Island is small, stay away from all edges

indicators.note: keeping away from all edges means only the inside letters are used

parts.note: small without its first and last letters
stay without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: The island is tiny, so keep clear of the cliffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is a Mediterranean island nation south of Sicily.

clue.text: Way to eat cold cut

indicators.note: to eat something is to take it inside, so the road word holds one letter

parts.note: a lane is a way or road
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A method of eating sliced cold meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To lance is to cut open with a sharp blade, as a doctor lances a boil.

clue.text: Hooked implement angler cast catches carp's tail

indicators.note: catches means holds within, so one letter goes inside the rearranged word

parts.note: the last letter of carp

explanation.definitionFit: A grapnel is a small anchor or grappling iron with several hooks or claws.

clue.text: Have facial hair trimmed

parts.note: a beard is facial hair

explanation.surface: Get your beard tidied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have' looks like an instruction, but it is the definition: to bear a child is to have it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bear can mean to carry or possess, or to give birth to, both senses of have.

clue.text: Drink dodgy lager, European beverage

parts.note: gin is a drink

parts.note: taken as written; the fodder
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' wants to be the definition, but it supplies GIN; the definition is at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger ale is a fizzy ginger-flavoured soft drink, so it is a beverage.

clue.text: Started game on table without money

definitions.meaning: first meaning: made the opening shot in snooker or pool, which is called the break

parts.note: to water something is to wet it

explanation.definitionFit: To be in a stew is an idiom for being in a state of worry or difficulty.

parts.note: fortune and chance both mean luck

a lord is a noble
